mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the prior 6 months increases discount rates, lowering the present value of future equity cash flows and thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for at least 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar rate hike periods, or FEDFUNDS deceleration reverses before 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% while PAYEMS increases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day backtest shows no statistically significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% yoy for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under the trigger are flat or negative, and detrended P&L shows no mean reversion.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month followed by a rebound suggests cyclical softening, which can precede a risk-off reaction in equity markets and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -2% followed by > 2% increase in the subsequent month
failure_condition: More than 40% of similar bottoms result in positive 20-day returns, or the rebound in INDPRO is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 1%, it indicates a shift toward rate easing, lowering real discount rates and increasing the present value of equity cash flows, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under this condition are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a healthier labor market, which can boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 5% while PAYEMS increases by 2% or more
failure_condition: Empirical power of the signal is weak (R-squared < 0.2) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for four consecutive months indicates disinflation, which can reduce the Fed's need for tightening and support equity valuations, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during similar low-inflation episodes are not significantly different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) shows a double-digit decline in two consecutive months followed by no rebound, it signals a deepening supply-side weakness that can trigger risk aversion and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month changes are both < -10% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: More than 60% of such events result in positive 20-day returns, or the market quickly recovers within 5 days.
